newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge awards $601 million against Meineke.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge awards $601 million against Meineke.

text.p: A federal judge has awarded Meineke muffler franchisees nearly $601 million in damages, one of the biggest awards of its kind, after a jury found Meineke had misused advertising fees, plaintiffs' lawyers said Thursday.

The award, which tripled the original jury verdict of $197 million and added interest, was also one of the biggest awards against a British company in the United States, lawyers for the franchisees said. Meineke is owned by GKN Plc, a maker of auto parts and other products, based in Britain.

The four-year-old lawsuit had accused Meineke, one of the nation's biggest muffler suppliers, of improperly taking millions of dollars for its own use from an advertising fund built up by franchisees.
The jury found last month after a six-week trial that Meineke had committed fraud by taking the money in breach of contracts with franchisees.

U.S. District Court Judge Robert D. Potter tripled the jury's Dec. 18 finding on compensatory damages. The original decision also had awarded another $150 million in punitive damages, now folded into the judge's award of $600.97 million.
The jury's award was based on lost profits from money improperly taken from the fund. It also found GKN, Meineke's parent, and affilates liable.
The award affects 2,500 franchisees included in the class-action. The suit was filed in December 1993 and the trial began last Nov. 6.

"We are very pleased with the court's decision," said Mark Zuckerman, president of the Association of Meineke Dealers, a franchisee group. "This is the largest award yet in franchise litigation and it will strengthen the franchising system."
Wayne Mack, a lawyer for the franchisees, said the judgment had far-reaching implications for franchisees and dealerships across the country.

"Our courts are leveling the playing field for small business owners. A new franchise opens every eight minutes in this country. Franchisees invest their life savings in these businesses and they deserve fair and honest treatment from franchisors."
Officials at Charlotte, N.C.-based Meineke were not immediately available for comment.
GKN Chief Executive C.K. Chow said in London before the ruling that the company believed Meineke would have a strong case on appeal. He said GKN had made no provision for the litigation.
GKN said last month it expected the award to be 30 percent lower than the $740 million it had originally feared. The company has cash reserves of about $850 million.
